title: Two Reports from Harbin
synopsis: Two newspapers tell An Jung-geun's story in two ways.
goal: Find out which report is true, and what An Jung-geun really called out.

notes: Played as two records compared (RecordsScene): the two papers agree on the date, the place and the name, and disagree only on what he called out.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheets of c07_paper_a.webp and c07_paper_b.webp (picture.measuredOn): each blank sheet's four corners; Paper A a wide folded sheet (flat 340x340), Paper B a tall sheet (flat 340x460, rows spread to fill it).
Both papers are made up (dossier fiction). Their words are the app's text over blank sheets: no writing in any picture.
Puzzle kind chosen by hand: the season spread assigns Case 07 a record comparison (PART 10 brief); Mrs. Kang's note asks for the one line that is not the same.

clueInputs.note: Bongsu's water-drop note of 1907: the same small water drop.
Lady Han's water drop of 1895: three keepers, one mark.

expressions: One line is not the same.

play.title: Two Papers on the Table
story: Two newspaper reports lie on Mrs. Kang's table.
Folded inside one is a small note with a water drop.
play.letterIntro: Mrs. Kang's note, in the King's letters, says:
play.letter:
Detective,
Two papers came today. They should agree.
Read both, line by line. One line is not the same.
Only one writer was on the platform.
— Kang
play.question: Which line does not match?
hints: Read the four lines of each paper, one by one.
The date, the place and the name agree. Look at the last line.
play.successMessage: The papers do not agree on what he called out!
transition: One paper says he called out nothing.
The other says he called out, "Korea, hurrah!"
Mrs. Kang nods. "Ask Mr. Pak. He carries bags at the station."

feedback.date:date: Both papers say 26 OCTOBER. Look for a line that differs.
feedback.place:place: Both papers say HARBIN STATION. Read on.
feedback.name:name: Both papers give the same name. Read the last line.

play.title: The Noon Train
story: Mr. Pak drinks his tea by the window.
He saw the Evening Sheet's writer that day.
"Put my day in order," he says. "Then you will see."
play.letter:
The tea room opened at 7:00.
That morning, before the noon train, I was on the platform with the bags.
The Evening Sheet's writer came on the noon train, at 12:00.
After the noon train, a traveller told him a story over tea.
He wrote his report at this table, after the story.
The Evening Sheet was printed at 5:00 PM.
A goods train came too. It does not matter.
play.question: Put Mr. Pak's day in order.
hints: Find the words before and after in Mr. Pak's day.
The goods train does not matter. Set it aside.
play.successMessage: The writer came at noon. He was never on the platform!
transition: Paper A came from a story told over tea.
Paper B came from a man on the platform.
"And I was on the platform too," Mr. Pak says quietly.
play.orderFeedback: Read Mr. Pak's words again. When did the writer come?

play.title: What Mr. Pak Heard

I was on the platform that morning. I heard him.
He did not run. He did not ask anyone for money.
He called out, "Korea, hurrah!"
He called out for his country, not for himself.

objectives: Find the line where the papers disagree.
Find out where Paper A's story came from.
Show the writer which report is true.
intro: Late October, 1909. You stay at Mrs. Kang's Korean inn in Harbin.
On 26 October, at Harbin Station, An Jung-geun killed Itō Hirobumi of Japan.
Everyone in Harbin is talking about it.
Two newspapers on Mrs. Kang's table tell his story in two ways.
play.caseSummary: Paper A was written from a story told over tea. Mr. Pak was on the platform: An Jung-geun called out, "Korea, hurrah!", not for money. Mrs. Kang kept the true report. In prison, An Jung-geun wrote about Korea's independence and peace in East Asia.

notes: Season 5 Case 07 (PART 10, 2026-11-06). Set days after 26 October 1909: the player never sees or helps with the act; it is told once, plainly, in the intro and the reveal.
The two papers, Mr. Sorin, Mr. Pak and Mrs. Kang's inn are made up. An Jung-geun does not appear: he is spoken of only, with checked facts (h1-h3).
No portrait of An Jung-geun is planned: he is never on stage.
